description:
Create a Sentry cron monitor.

Use this tool when you need to:
- Monitor a scheduled job (cron job, scheduled task) for missed, failed, or slow runs
- Set up a cron monitor before instrumenting check-ins

Set `schedule` to exactly one crontab or interval schedule. Check-ins must still be sent by the job (SDK `monitor_config`/check-ins or `sentry monitor run`) using the returned slug.
workflowIds optionally connect existing notification Alerts without modifying them. Use find_alert_rules(kind='issue') to find workflow IDs.
If the returned status is `disabled` but you did not request that, the organization has no cron monitor seat available. Tell the user; the monitor ignores check-ins until a seat frees up and it is enabled.
After an error or timeout, use find_monitors with the name and project before retrying; creation is not idempotent.

<examples>
create_monitor(organizationSlug='my-organization', projectSlug='backend', name='Nightly Import', schedule={ type: 'crontab', crontab: '0 3 * * *' }, timezone='America/Los_Angeles', checkInMargin=5, maxRuntime=30)
create_monitor(organizationSlug='my-organization', projectSlug='backend', name='Queue Drain', schedule={ type: 'interval', value: 15, unit: 'minute' })
</examples>

checkInMargin.description: Minutes after the expected time before a check-in counts as missed. Sentry treats 0 as 1.

failureIssueThreshold.description: Consecutive failed or missed check-ins before an issue opens.

maxRuntime.description: Minutes a check-in may stay in progress before it fails.

organizationSlug.description: The organization's slug. You can find a existing list of organizations you have access to using the `find_organizations()` tool.

projectSlug.description: The project's slug. You can find a list of existing projects in an organization using the `find_projects()` tool.

recoveryThreshold.description: Consecutive successful check-ins before the issue resolves.

anyOf.description: The region URL for the organization you're querying, if known. For Sentry's Cloud Service (sentry.io), this is typically the region-specific URL like 'https://us.sentry.io'. For self-hosted Sentry installations, this parameter is usually not needed and should be omitted. You can find the correct regionUrl from the organization details using the `find_organizations()` tool.

schedule.description: Monitor schedule: exactly one of `{ type: 'crontab', crontab: '0 3 * * *' }` or `{ type: 'interval', value: 15, unit: 'minute' }`.

crontab.description: Five-field crontab schedule or `@` alias, e.g. `0 3 * * *` or `@daily`. Seconds fields are not supported.

slug.description: Optional monitor slug used by check-ins. Derived from the name when omitted.

status.description: Monitor status. Disabled monitors ignore check-ins.

timezone.description: tz database timezone for the schedule, e.g. `UTC`.

workflowIds.description: Existing notification Alert IDs to connect.

name: create_monitor

checkInMargin.description: Minutes before a late check-in counts as missed.

failureIssueThreshold.description: Consecutive failures before an issue opens.

maxRuntime.description: Minutes a check-in may stay in progress.

recoveryThreshold.description: Consecutive successes before the issue resolves.

slug.description: Monitor slug that check-ins must use.

status.description: `active` or `disabled`; unrequested `disabled` means no seat was available.

title: Create Cron Monitor
